props.contract: Logical left shift: r0 = r0 << r1, with a signed count. For r1 < 0 it returns the input unchanged; for r1 >= 32 it returns 0. The shifted value is necessarily r0 because paths 28..31 use the encoding and #imm,r0 and cannot target another register. It clobbers r1; r2 is preserved on the stack. It does not write global RAM; memory accesses are the stack and a byte read from table 0x2219c. T is not a contractual output.

props.summary: Diagnostic runtime-record byte-1 bit-7 predicate. It addresses ffff5718 + 3*index and returns that bit as a Boolean.
note: Test runtime diagnostic record byte 1 bit 7 with minus-one sentinel support
Indices 0x71 and 0x123 are exact P2119 and P1238 descriptors in 0005096c.
props.contract: Input r4 is interpreted as a signed 16-bit record index. Index -1 returns zero without reading RAM; other indices return byte1.bit7 of the selected three-byte record.

note: The real predicate is executed with natural returns for caller ids 012d and 013f, yielding byte1 addresses ffff5aa0 and ffff5ad6. Direct contexts separately vary all record bytes and full R4 upper words; a low-word ffff sentinel returns zero without a record read. Full R4 is preserved and nonsentinel pointer arithmetic consumes its signed low word. Other signed indices, array extent, diagnostic production and hardware identity remain outside this bounded proof. Existing generic predicate contract and other caller evidence are unchanged.

props.summary: Final signed timing coordinate in degBTDC written by 0004dbe8 after mode-dependent limits and overrides. Before the rate limiter and bounds it is ffff11da=clamp(ffff12d6+gated ffff564c, ROM8[0x8221]=-7, ROM8[0x821e]=50), and the full chain is ffff23f1 + (low7-64) + (ffff1a7d-64) - ffff23c5 - ffff12dc - ffff15ea + ffff134a - ffff11af + ffff2356 - ffff11f9 - ffff1ff6 + ffff564c with every coefficient 1. FUN 0004df82 transforms the result into ffff2022 and passes it to APC scheduler 0002a892. J1979 Mode 01 PID 0x0E in FUN 00035856 returns clamp((ROM8[0x83d5]-ffff2022)*2, -128..127)+128, which is 2*ffff11d4+128 on the normal path.
note: The normal transform is uint8(110-uint8(ffff11d4)). In the instrumented 1.11 target capture, this identity holds outside the Rolling Launch late override. During that override ffff11d4 remains the upstream stock coordinate while ffff2022 carries the effective command. The -7 bound is not universal across diagnostic and fallback modes; physical degree scale and pulse polarity remain hardware boundaries. J1979 defines PID 0x0E as A/2-64 degrees before TDC, so the ECU declares one count of this coordinate as one crank degree of advance; the physical spark angle remains a hardware item.

props.summary: Six-row 7mfk reference bank updated or wholly reset by the RAM-only learner.

note: The complete learner binds six rows of eight uint16 words, 16 bytes per row and 96 bytes total. Normal legal channel c in 1..6 updates only row ffff2178+16*(c-1). Either real queried diagnostic bit7 set copies the raw reset word to all 48 words, including sibling rows. The normal old word is zero-extended before multiplication; the row footprint and full-bank extent are exact executed storage claims without physical channel order or acquisition semantics.

props.note: With selector bit3 set, MOV.B 0004a13a supplies selected channel c from ffff1ff4+0x14f. Normal learning uses declared legal c in 1..6. With selector bit3 clear, MOV.B 0004a17e supplies selected channel c, then normal learning constrains its zero-extended value to the declared legal domain 1..6. The other channel byte is independently different. The caller channel-zero guard and physical cylinder order are not executed or inferred here.

Either queried diagnostic result set selects forced full-bank reset: for every j in 0..47, to = ROM16[0x00009282]. All 48 raw words receive this value, not only the selected row. The normal path does not read this scalar. Artificial reset words are separate contexts.

Normal learning reads unsigned v=RAM16[ffff20c2+2*i] with i=x in 0..7. EXTU.W 0004a1c2 precedes multiplication. Both real diagnostic results must be clear; forced reset does not read the sample vector. Acquisition and digital-bin production are not executed by this CPU-only learner.

Normal learning uses byte W and coefficients W and 255-W. q=floor((W*v+(255-W)*old)/256); the conditional +1 is taken only if q<old. The declared uint16/byte domain has q<=65279 and result<=65280, so the final upper-clamp taken arm is unreachable. Artificial weights are labelled independently of stock bytes.

On normal learning, the loaded reference base and channel select eight old uint16 words; EXTU.W zero-extends each before the weighted multiply. Only the selected row is rewritten. Forced reset reads no old numeric reference value and copies all 48 reset words. Natural return and per-case sibling isolation are independently checked.

The real queries use ids 012d and 013f. Both clear selects normal eight-word learning; either byte1.bit7 set selects all 48 reference words for forced reset. If the first result is set the second query is skipped by the genuine code. This source/branch contract makes no direct call-count observation, diagnostic producer, acquisition or hardware claim.

ROM8[00008b3d].bit3 clear selects primary ffff11de; set selects alternate ffff2143. Legal channel c is 1..6. Every unrelated selector bit is independently varied and preserved. The complete learner reads the scalar and channel bytes, without executing acquisition or its caller zero-guard.

With either result set, the independent reset view for j in 0..47 is to = ROM16[0x00009282] and writes all 48 words/96 bytes. The maximum normal result is 65280 for the declared uint16/byte-weight domain; the upper-clamp taken arm is unreachable. All other 64k RAM, samples, channels, diagnostic records and calibration/pool bytes are preserved per case. Acquisition, the static caller and full evaluator dispatch are not executed.
